newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's powerful CPP allies with smaller party.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's powerful CPP allies with smaller party.

text.p: Cambodia's volatile political scene polarised further on Monday when Hun Sen's powerful Cambodian People's Party signed an alliance with a former battlefield foe.
Second Prime Minister Hun Sen and the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) signed the cooperation agreement during a ceremony at CPP headquarters attended by top officials from both sides.
"This is not the establishment of a front (of parties to fight coming elections) but this is a cooperation pact ... to keep social and political stability," Hun Sen said.

Analysts said the move was a response to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh's plans to form an alliance between his FUNCINPEC party and the opposition Khmer Nation Party (KNP) and a wing of the divided Buddhist Liberal Democratic Party (BLDP).

Hun Sen said the CPP would also sign agreements with "not less than five parties and not more than 10", including a rival wing of the BLDP led by Information Minister Ieng Mouly. The analysts said the two main coalition parties were marshalling their forces ahead of local and general elections due by the end of 1998 and warned that pre-election alliances could exacerbate their strained relations.

Ties between the two parties have deteriorated due to FUNCINPEC demands for more power to reflect their narrow 1993 victory at the polls and efforts by both premiers to win over the allegiance of thousands of defectors from the rebel Khmer Rouge.
